executive_summary:
[DEMO MODE (SYNTHETIC EVIDENCE)] Security Assessment Report — Automated Demonstration Security Assessment

This security assessment identified 7 potential findings with an overall risk rating of CRITICAL.
Severity breakdown: 2 critical, 1 high, 2 medium, 2 low.

IMPORTANT: This assessment was conducted in demonstration mode using synthetic evidence. All findings are hypothetical and should be validated through actual security testing before taking remediation action.

Immediate attention is recommended for critical and high-severity findings. A detailed remediation plan with prioritized actions is provided in the findings section.
methodology:
This assessment was conducted in DEMO MODE using the following methodology:
1. Scope Validation — Verified assessment scope against authorized targets
2. Synthetic Reconnaissance — Analyzed predefined synthetic asset inventory
3. Vulnerability Analysis — Applied synthetic findings based on common security weaknesses
4. Evidence Validation — Checked finding consistency and detected duplicates
5. Risk Assessment — Applied deterministic severity rules based on finding characteristics
6. Report Generation — Compiled findings into structured report format

NOTE: No live scanning, network probes, or external API calls were performed. All evidence is synthetic and for demonstration purposes only.

findings.title: Outdated TLS Configuration
findings.description: The web server supports TLS 1.0 and 1.1, which are deprecated protocols with known cryptographic weaknesses. An attacker in a network position could potentially exploit protocol downgrade attacks to intercept encrypted communications.
findings.evidence: Synthetic configuration review: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 protocols enabled in nginx.conf
findings.remediation: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 in the web server configuration. Enable only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with strong cipher suites (e.g., ECDHE+AESGCM). Test with tools like SSL Labs.

findings.title: Dependency with Known Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
findings.description: The API server uses a dependency (synthetic-lib v1.2.3) with a known remote code execution vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker could send specially crafted requests to execute arbitrary code on the server.
findings.evidence: Synthetic dependency audit: synthetic-lib@1.2.3 flagged with known RCE vulnerability
findings.remediation: Update synthetic-lib to version 1.2.5 or later. If immediate update is not possible, implement Web Application Firewall rules to block known exploit patterns. Review application code that uses the vulnerable library for additional hardening.

findings.title: Database Exposed to Non-Application Networks
findings.description: The PostgreSQL database on port 5432 is accessible from network segments beyond the application tier. This violates the principle of least privilege and could allow direct database access from compromised hosts in adjacent network zones.
findings.evidence: Synthetic network topology review: database port open to 192.168.1.0/24 (wider than application tier)
findings.remediation: Restrict database access to application-tier hosts only using host-based firewall rules (iptables/nftables) or network segmentation (VLANs). Update pg_hba.conf to allow connections only from the application server IP.

findings.title: Overly Permissive CORS Configuration
findings.description: The API server has CORS configured with Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to '*', allowing any origin to make cross-origin requests. Combined with credential handling, this could enable cross-site request forgery or data exfiltration from authenticated sessions.
findings.evidence: Synthetic configuration review: CORS origin set to wildcard '*' in Express middleware
findings.remediation: Replace the wildcard CORS origin with a specific allowlist of trusted domains. Ensure Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is not used with wildcard origins. Implement proper CORS validation in the API middleware.

findings.title: Database Management Interface Exposed
findings.description: pgAdmin is accessible on port 8443 of the database server. Administrative database management interfaces should not be exposed to the network and should require VPN or bastion host access.
findings.evidence: Synthetic port scan: pgAdmin web interface detected on port 8443
findings.remediation: Restrict pgAdmin access to localhost or a dedicated management network. Require VPN access for remote database administration. If pgAdmin is not needed, remove or disable it entirely.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers
findings.description: The web application does not set critical HTTP security headers including X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, and Content-Security-Policy. This increases the attack surface for clickjacking, MIME-type confusion, and cross-site scripting attacks.
findings.evidence: Synthetic HTTP response analysis: security headers absent from server responses
findings.remediation: Configure the web server to include: X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000, and a restrictive Content-Security-Policy.

findings.title: Verbose Error Messages Exposing Internal Details
findings.description: API error responses include detailed stack traces, internal file paths, and database query information. This information could help an attacker understand the application architecture and identify specific vulnerabilities to target.
findings.evidence: Synthetic API response review: error responses contain traceback and internal paths
findings.remediation: Implement generic error responses for production environments. Log detailed error information server-side only. Ensure debug mode is disabled in production. Use a centralized error handler that sanitizes responses.

limitations:
• DEMO MODE: All findings are synthetic and for demonstration purposes only.
• OUT-OF-SCOPE ASSET: Finding 'Outdated TLS Configuration' asset 'demo.lab.local' does not map to approved targets.
• Real dependency manifest needed for dependency audit
• Excluded targets strictly prohibited from testing: 192.168.1.1
• No live network scanning performed
• OUT-OF-SCOPE ASSET: Finding 'Dependency with Known Remote Code Execution Vulnerability' asset 'api.lab.local' does not map to approved targets.
• Live TLS scan results needed to confirm TLS findings
• OUT-OF-SCOPE ASSET: Finding 'Missing HTTP Security Headers' asset 'demo.lab.local' does not map to approved targets.
• OUT-OF-SCOPE ASSET: Finding 'Database Exposed to Non-Application Networks' asset 'db.lab.local:5432' does not map to approved targets.
• OUT-OF-SCOPE ASSET: Finding 'Verbose Error Messages Exposing Internal Details' asset 'api.lab.local' does not map to approved targets.
• Demo mode — analysis uses synthetic evidence only
• Network scan needed to confirm port exposure findings
• Actual HTTP response headers needed for header analysis
• OUT-OF-SCOPE ASSET: Finding 'Overly Permissive CORS Configuration' asset 'api.lab.local' does not map to approved targets.
• OUT-OF-SCOPE ASSET: Finding 'Database Management Interface Exposed' asset 'db.lab.local:8443' does not map to approved targets.
remediation_priorities: Priority 1 [CRITICAL]: Outdated TLS Configuration — Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 in the web server configuration. Enable only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with strong cipher suites (e.g., ECDHE+AESGCM). Test with tools like SSL Labs.

Priority 2 [CRITICAL]: Dependency with Known Remote Code Execution Vulnerability — Update synthetic-lib to version 1.2.5 or later. If immediate update is not possible, implement Web Application Firewall rules to block known exploit patterns. Review application code that uses the vulnerable library for additional hardening.

Priority 3 [HIGH]: Database Exposed to Non-Application Networks — Restrict database access to application-tier hosts only using host-based firewall rules (iptables/nftables) or network segmentation (VLANs). Update pg_hba.conf to allow connections only from the application server IP.

Priority 4 [MEDIUM]: Overly Permissive CORS Configuration — Replace the wildcard CORS origin with a specific allowlist of trusted domains. Ensure Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is not used with wildcard origins. Implement proper CORS validation in the API middleware.

Priority 5 [MEDIUM]: Database Management Interface Exposed — Restrict pgAdmin access to localhost or a dedicated management network. Require VPN access for remote database administration. If pgAdmin is not needed, remove or disable it entirely.

Priority 6 [LOW]: Missing HTTP Security Headers — Configure the web server to include: X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000, and a restrictive Content-Security-Policy.

Priority 7 [LOW]: Verbose Error Messages Exposing Internal Details — Implement generic error responses for production environments. Log detailed error information server-side only. Ensure debug mode is disabled in production. Use a centralized error handler that sanitizes responses.
